narrative: The PR changed filterFiles to return {reviewed, excluded} and missed the caller in eval/run-case.js (F1/F2). The fix for that caller left the wiring untested, which the agent admitted and deferred, so round 2 existed only to ask for that test (F5). Round 3's F6 was the very false positive the PR targets: the dist rebuild was hidden by EXCLUDE_PATTERNS. The agent's response, naming the withheld paths, was a design change, and round 4 found two consequences of it: the unbounded log sink (F7) and the newly exposed scout scoping hole (F9). The review hit the 5-round cap, so the fixes for round 4 got no GitHub review; a local review then caught a real bug in the F9 fix.
guidance_observations: The agent's original caller search was limited to src/ and scripts/; a repo-wide search for callers would have prevented round 0's only real defect.
Deferring a gap the agent itself had named ('residual gap... out of scope') cost a full review round on the next push.
A substantial prompt redesign during review (4313bb7) behaves like new feature code and drew new findings, so it needs its own sweep of every sink and consumer of the changed value before pushing.
Running scripts/local-review.js after the round cap caught a real bug, which suggests running it before each push rather than only once the GitHub rounds are used up.
